- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then drop too sharply, missing sustained upward momentum.
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., 75+ → 80+), then undercorrects, failing to account for mean reversion.
- Model underestimates late-period price declines (last 5–10 days of 30d), particularly when true values show downward correction.
- Forecast bias is stronger in high-volatility periods (e.g., 2025-01-07 to 2025-01-10), suggesting model lacks adaptive response to regime shifts.
- Model fails to capture “late-cycle” mean reversion — overestimates peak, then underestimates subsequent pullback.
- Forecasts show lagged response to recent price movements — model reacts to past trends rather than current momentum.
- In low-volatility periods (e.g., 2024-05-10), model underestimates upward bias and fails to anticipate minor spikes.
